conventions: Preposition plus construct noun is split throughout this chapter wherever the ASV spends an English word on each morpheme - LIFNE -> in the sight (4.3), BE-DEREKH -> in the way (4.11), BE-TOKH -> in the midst (4.21) - and fused under rule 30 only where a single English rendering covers the pair, ME-ALAYW -> from (4.15) and LE-NOKHAH -> right on (4.25). Rule 30's corpus counts for LIFNE -> before and for a preposition with TOKH or QEREV -> among do not reach these places, because the ASV has not written those renderings here; read what the ASV wrote before reaching for the precedent. The fused units head on the noun carrying the lexeme, or on the governing morpheme standing first where neither noun carries content the other lacks (rule 23), and the split units give each morpheme the word written for it.

Where a coordinating waw stands between two verbs and the ASV's only and is written inside one verb's own multi-word adverbial rendering, that and belongs to the verb's unit and the waw is unrepresented. HOLEKH WA-OR -> shineth more and more (4.18) gives more and more whole to HOLEKH, the progression verb rendered as an adverb under rule 56, whose one-rendering sentence leaves no part of such an expression to a neighbouring morpheme, and leaves the waw with no connective written for it under rule 14. Do not divide the expression to give the waw something to hold: the second more would then answer to no morpheme. This is the chapter's one BSB disagreement that is not a documented convention difference.
report: All 31 candidate lemma groups were read and none is a split: every bucket with two treatments turns on a word the ASV itself wrote differently, or on a source difference. REGEL is a chain rectum at 4.26 (of thy feet) and a bare object at 4.27 (thy foot); the article HA is written at 4.18 (the perfect day) and unwritten at 4.13/4.19; IM LO fuses identically at both 4.16 occurrences, headed on the negative, and only the English word differs (except, unless); BEN takes a supplied O at 4.10 because the ASV writes one and none at 4.1/4.20 because it does not; SUR is Put away at 4.24 and Remove at 4.27; the LE and BE buckets are the ASV's own choice of to/unto and in/into.

The dump was read end to end for the splits the lemma table is blind to, since it is keyed by source lemma and shows no added units. The four added units - my (4.1), therefore (4.7), her (4.13), some (4.16) - were each checked against every parallel construction in the chapter, and the converse sweep found no supplied word folded into a licensing morpheme where a parallel verse marked the same word added. The her of let her not go (4.13) is the one contestable case: no object morpheme stands on TEREF, and rule 25's resumed-referent paragraph governs a subject rather than an object, so rule 44 leaves it added; the verse note already names the competing reading, and every other object pronoun in the chapter (4.6 twice, 4.9, 4.13 Keep her, 4.21) answers to a written suffix.

Head choices are uniform across the chapter: a light verb plus complement heads on the complement (4.8 honor, 4.10 many, 4.13 hold, 4.16 evil, 4.24 far, 4.25 straight, 4.26 level), a bare particle leaves the head on the verb (4.15 pass on, 4.24 Put away), and a substantive with a supplied generic heads on the lexeme-bearing word (4.3 only, 4.7 principal, 4.14 evil, 4.27 right). Determiners are counted the same way in both English orders of an attributive chain - the construct takes the single supplied one at 4.18 (the dawning light) and 4.24 (a wayward mouth) - while a present article takes the written the first (4.18 the perfect day) and each noun takes the one standing before its own word (4.1 the instruction of a father).

The one line the chapter drew that the contract does not draw for it is where preposition plus construct noun fuses. It splits wherever the ASV spends a word on each morpheme (4.3 in the sight, 4.11 in the way, 4.21 in the midst) and fuses only where one rendering covers the pair (4.15 from, 4.25 right on). That is rule 30 applied consistently, but it runs against the corpus counts rule 30 itself cites for LIFNE and BETOKH, so it is recorded as a convention.

BSB disagreements: 4.2 (dative LE left unrepresented before a bare English indirect object) and 4.20 (paragogic he) are the documented convention differences rules 40 and 32 name in their own text, and neither is an error. 4.18 (the waw of HOLEKH WA-OR) is a genuine judgment rather than a convention: the ASV's only and stands inside more and more, which rule 56 takes whole as the auxiliary verb's one adverbial rendering, leaving no part of it to a neighbouring morpheme, so the waw is unrepresented under rule 14. BSB gives the and to the waw. The chapter's reading is the better one, because the alternative leaves the second more with no morpheme to answer to; the verse note names it and it is recorded as a convention.

No promotions. Everything this chapter decided is already decided by rules 14, 17, 29, 30, 44, 46, 52 and 56 as they stand - including the 4.18 hendiadys, which rule 56's one-rendering sentence settles - and a rule restating them would be padding. Verdict no-change; 305 units, all ids partitioned once, no patches.
